extractedItems.title: Options After Hitting Into a Red Penalty Area
extractedItems.question: Your ball lands in a red penalty area. Which of these is an extra option you have (compared to a yellow penalty area)?

choices.text: Play the ball as it lies, if possible.
Take a drop within two club-lengths of the entry point, for one penalty stroke.
Replay from the original spot only.
Drop anywhere on the course you like, for one penalty stroke.

extractedItems.explanation: With a red penalty area, you can drop within two club-lengths of where the ball last crossed the edge, with a penalty stroke. This is not allowed in a yellow penalty area.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A young golfer standing near the edge of a red-staked penalty area, holding a ball and preparing to drop it within two club-lengths of the spot where the ball entered the water.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Golfer about to drop a ball next to a red-staked penalty area by a stream.

extractedItems.title: What Should You Do After Losing a Ball in a Red Penalty Area?
extractedItems.question: If your ball goes into a red penalty area and you can't find it, what are your basic options?

choices.text: Replay the shot from your previous spot with a penalty stroke.
Drop a ball within two club-lengths of where it crossed into the penalty area, with a penalty stroke.
Drop a ball anywhere you want with no penalty.
Take a drop on a straight line back from the hole through the entry point, with a penalty stroke.

extractedItems.explanation: You can replay the shot, drop within two club-lengths of the entry point, or take a drop on the line back from the hole. All options cost one penalty stroke.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teen golfer near a red-staked penalty area considering their options after a ball went into the water, looking at possible drop areas.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Golfer looking at drop options beside a red penalty area.

extractedItems.title: Knowing When Local Rules Offer Extra Options
extractedItems.question: True or false? Local Rules at some courses may give you extra dropping options in penalty areas, such as a special dropping zone.

choices.text: True
False
Only if you ask the referee

extractedItems.explanation: Local Rules can allow extra dropping options, such as a special dropping zone, beyond the standard rules.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A girl golfer reading a notice board with Local Rules near a penalty area with red stakes.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Golfer reading Local Rules near a red penalty area.

reviewedItems.title: Options After Hitting Into a Red Penalty Area
reviewedItems.question: Your ball lands in a red penalty area. Which of the following relief options is available for a red penalty area but not for a yellow penalty area?

choices.text: Play the ball as it lies, if possible.
Drop a ball within two club-lengths of where it last crossed into the area, for one penalty stroke.
Replay the shot from your previous spot, for one penalty stroke.
Drop anywhere on the course for one penalty stroke.

reviewedItems.explanation: Only red penalty areas allow the option to drop a ball within two club-lengths of where it last crossed into the area, with a one-stroke penalty. This option is not allowed for yellow penalty areas.
reviewedItems.imagePrompt: A left-handed teen boy about to drop a ball within two club-lengths of the edge of a red-staked penalty area, with water clearly visible and red stakes marking the edge.
reviewedItems.imageAlt: Left-handed teen golfer preparing to drop a ball by a red-staked penalty area next to water.

reviewedItems.title: What Should You Do After Losing a Ball in a Red Penalty Area?
reviewedItems.question: If your ball goes into a red penalty area and you can't retrieve it, which relief options are allowed under the Rules (each for one penalty stroke)? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Replay your shot from the previous spot.
Drop a ball within two club-lengths of the point where it crossed into the penalty area.
Drop a ball anywhere you like on the course, with no penalty.
Drop a ball behind the penalty area, keeping the entry point between you and the hole.

reviewedItems.explanation: If your ball is lost in a red penalty area, you may: replay the shot, drop within two club-lengths of the entry point, or drop behind the penalty area on a straight line from the hole—each for one penalty stroke.
